record.paper_title: Open Problems Related to Algebraic Attacks on Stream Ciphers
record.original_question: For balanced Boolean functions of n variables, determine what proportion of them attain optimal algebraic immunity, meaning the maximum algebraic immunity allowed for that number of variables.

evidence.quote: However, both following problems are still open.
Open problem 6. Determine the proportion of balanced Boolean functions of n variables with optimal algebraic immunity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $\mathcal{B}_n$ denote the set of Boolean functions $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n \to \mathbb{F}_2$. For $f \in \mathcal{B}_n$, the algebraic immunity $\mathrm{AI}(f)$ is defined as the smallest positive integer $d$ such that there exists a nonzero function $g \in \mathcal{B}_n$ of algebraic degree at most $d$ with $fg = 0$ or $(f \oplus 1)g = 0$; equivalently, $\mathrm{AI}(f)$ is the minimum degree of a nonzero annihilator of $f$ or of $f \oplus 1$. It is known that $\mathrm{AI}(f) \leq \lceil n/2 \rceil$ for every $f \in \mathcal{B}_n$, and a function attaining this bound is said to have optimal algebraic immunity. A Boolean function $f$ is balanced if $|\{x \in \mathbb{F}_2^n : f(x) = 1\}| = 2^{n-1}$. Let $B_n$ denote the set of balanced Boolean functions of $n$ variables, and let $B_n^* \subseteq B_n$ denote the subset of those that have optimal algebraic immunity. Determine the proportion
$$ \rho(n) \;=\; \frac{|B_n^*|}{|B_n|}, $$
and in particular describe its asymptotic behavior as $n \to \infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search reveals extensive literature on constructions of balanced Boolean functions achieving optimal algebraic immunity, but no result giving the exact proportion or its asymptotic value among all balanced n-variable Boolean functions. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Balanced Boolean Functions with (Almost) Optimal Algebraic Immunity and Very High Nonlinearity
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of balanced Boolean functions with optimal AI, focusing on existence rather than density.

status_evidence.title: Finding More Boolean Functions with Maximum Algebraic Immunity Based on Univariate Polynomial Representation
status_evidence.snippet: Provides further families of functions with maximum AI; does not determine the proportion among balanced functions.
status_evidence.claim: No determination of the proportion is given.
